extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, policies and normative statements concerning how government, military and the press should handle publicity and information about missile/satellite tests, defense research organization, and related public-disclosure issues. Also includes related policy decisions from NATO and procedural points about nuclear plant commissioning reported in the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press should not report only successes / full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an implication in criticism of Vanguard test publicity that the public can be told only good news — an implication rejected: the press should not be limited to reporting only successes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'THIS IS AN IMPLICATION WHICH I DEEPLY RESENT AND FLATLY REJECT.' Context: press interest in launches mirrored public concern; reporters should provide full information rather than a one-sided 'only good news' narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-secrecy after failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials should resist calls for greater secrecy in reaction to a failure of a public scientific/military project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moss said he was glad Snyder did not succumb 'TO THE HYSTERIA CALLING MORE SECRECY' after the Vanguard failure — normative guidance to favor transparency over panic-driven secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic right to know — no complete blackout of non-security programs
rubrics_metrics.description: A democratic society cannot impose a complete blackout of information about non-security government programs; the public has a right to know government failures as well as successes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmented text: 'A DEMOCRATIC SOCIETY CANNOT ... A COMPLETE BLACKOUT OF ... NON-SECUR[ITY] PROGRAMS' and 'THE PEOPLE HAVE A RIGHT ... TO CONSIDER GOVERNMENT'S FAILURES' — supports policy that non-sensitive program information should be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of non-security defense information conditioned on public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about Defense Department programs of a non-security nature should be released when 'public interest required'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'NO RESPONSIBLE OFFICIAL ... PUBLIC INTEREST REQUIRED { RESPECT TO ANY DEFENSE DEPART- ... MENT PROGRAM OF A NON-SECURITY NATURE.' Implies a test of 'public interest' for disclosure of non-sensitive defense program details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press coordination to avoid national harm in reporting tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The press should adopt reporting policies for missile/satellite tests that avoid causing 'incalculable harm' to the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rep. Osmers: 'THE PRESS SHOULD GET TOGETHER AND ADOPT A POLICY OF REPORTING THESE TESTS THAT WILL NOT DO THE NATION THE INCALCULABLE HARM THAT THE VANGUARD REPORTING DID.' Guidance toward cooperative, responsible reporting (e.g., avoid sensational or premature disclosures that could harm national security or public confidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official announcements should be limited and non-technical
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense/launch authorities typically withhold detailed technical metrics in public statements, giving only limited, general descriptions of test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT ANNOUNCED ONLY THAT THE ATLAS HAD BEEN GIVEN "A LIMITED RANGE TEST OF SEVERAL HUNDRED ... FLOWN ITS PRESCRIBED COURSE, AND HAD LANDED IN A PRE-SELECTED IMPACT AREA.' Also: 'THE MISSILE TEST CENTER POLICY IS TO WITHHOLD EXACT DETAILS AS TO DISTANCE, HEIGHT, SPEED AND ACCURACY OF A TEST FLIGHT.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Missile Test Center policy — withhold exact test flight details
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy: withhold exact details (distance, height, speed, accuracy, even target size) of missile test flights from public release; these factors may vary with each test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit line: 'THE MISSILE TEST CENTER POLICY IS TO WITHHOLD EXACT DETAILS AS TO DISTANCE , HEIGHT, SPEED AND ACCURACY OF A TEST FLIGHT. THESE FACTORS, EVEN THE SIZE OF THE TARGET AREA, MAY VARY WITH EACH TEST.' Use this as the operational criterion for information release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public observation/site restrictions at launch areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Public viewing areas for launches may be subject to searches and bans on photography and certain equipment; restrictions are to be posted and enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign text cited: 'ALL VEHICLES ARE SUBJECT TO SEARCH WHILE ON GOVERNMENT PROPERTY. NO PHOTOGRAPHING ALLOWED. NO CAMERA OR SUPPORTING EQUIPMENT ALLOWED. NO FIREARMS, AMMUNITION OR EXPLOSIVES ALLOWED.' Practical guideline for site security and press conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clandestine or 'sneak' satellite launches
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers were suspicious of attempts to disguise an operational missile launch as a routine test in order to covertly place a satellite in orbit — such actions raise public and diplomatic concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: 'THE SUSPICION PERSISTED AMONG SOME OBSERVERS HERE THAT THE ARMY WAS PLANNING TO PUT UP ITS JUPITER-C IN A SNEAK ATTEMPT TO LAUNCH A SATELLITE.' Normative implication: avoid covert use of tests to conceal strategic deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense R&D organization: avoid overlapping agencies; services should manage programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that armed services, not a new overlapping centralized agency, should develop their own missile programs under proper supervision; reduce overlap and simplify organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kimball: 'WE DON'T NEED ANY MORE OVERLAPPING ... WHAT WE NEED IS A SIMPLIFIED ORGANIZATION WHICH WILL LET THE ARMED SERVICES DEVELOP THEIR OWN PROGRAMS UNDER PROPER SUPERVISION.' Critique of creating an 'Advanced Research Projects Agency' for programs that are essentially service responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate research from operationalization and base requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and development (advanced research) should be separated from the operational task of making systems operational and dealing with base/operational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kimball: 'THESE PROGRAMS ARE CLEARLY MILITARY AND THE PROBLEM OF MAKING THEM OPERATIONAL BELONGS TO THE SERVICES, NOT TO AN ADVANCED RESEARCH AGENCY.' Also: 'DERE[N]ANG AND BASE REQUIREMENTS MUST BE SET APART FROM THE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT EFFORT.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for a high-level organization to find effective solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a call for a new kind of high-level organization charged with the task of reaching effective solutions to missile problems, distinct from overlapping departmental structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kimball's phrasing: 'WHAT WE NEED IS NOT SO MUCH ANOTHER ORGANIZATION AS A NEW KIND OF ORGANIZATION AT HIGH LEVEL - AN ORGANIZATION WHICH WILL ... TASK OF REACHING AN EFFECTIVE SOLUTION TO OUR MISSILE PROBLEMS.' Emphasizes strategic leadership rather than more bureaucratic overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: establish nuclear stockpiles and make them readily available
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision: stockpiles of nuclear warheads for various arms will be set up and made readily available in case of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the NATO summit summary of major decisions; functions as a security posture standard for alliance preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: place intermediate-range ballistic missiles (IRBMs) at the disposal of the Supreme Allied Commander
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision to deploy IRBMs under the control of the Supreme Allied Commander as part of NATO force posture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarized under 'MEDIUM RANGE MISSILES' in the NATO decisions; a criterion for command and control structure of deployed systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: integration and standardization of conventional forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration and standardization will take place especially in air and naval defense, logistic support, and composition and equipment of conventional forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages standardization across NATO members to increase interoperability — a metric for future procurement and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: reopen disarmament talks and remain open to negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Soviet Union rejected prior proposals, NATO will explore reopening disarmament talks within the UN framework and welcomes meetings of foreign ministers (including Russia) to discuss disarmament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the political/diplomatic posture: combine military preparedness with readiness for negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: call on Soviet pledge for German reunification
rubrics_metrics.description: NATO calls on the Soviet government to honor its 1955 pledge to permit reunification of Germany by means of free elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A political demand included in alliance statements; functions as a diplomatic criterion for Soviet behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: scientific cooperation, training and pooling of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a NATO science committee to promote training of scientists, pool facilities and information, and study proposals (e.g., a French plan for a foundation for scientific research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guideline for alliance-level scientific capacity-building and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: set up technical groups and appoint general technical advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a technical group to study arms development, graduate research and range posture; appoint a general technical advisor for the NATO secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational measure to improve technical oversight and harmonize research agendas across NATO members.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO policy: emphasize stability in the Middle East and cooperate with African nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers declared stability in the Middle East vital to world peace and pledged to cooperate with African countries and peoples to promote peace and independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad foreign-policy criterion tied to alliance strategic priorities noted in the summit summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuclear plant commissioning practice (Shippingport example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioning practice for the Shippingport nuclear plant: begin with small test output tied into the grid after test operation, gradually step up production to full capacity; AEC supervision; projected fuel life and core replacement planning; cost-per-kilowatt estimates considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: initial output ~5,000 kW on a test basis, stepped up to 60,000 kW; 'THE NUCLEAR REACTOR HAS BEEN IN TEST OPERATION' and AEC/Westinghouse/Duquesne roles referenced; guidance on cautious, supervised ramp-up and cost-awareness.
